C5-01.title: Reading their formation
C5-01.scene: The opponent at the back hits and runs forward.
C5-01.cue: One player is already at the net.
C5-01.question: Who do you watch now?

answer.why: The one who moves changes the formation. When the back player comes in, they'll both be up soon.
answer.caption: You lobbed over their heads

lo.why: The net player matters too, but the one moving right now is changing the formation.
lo.caption: Cut off at the net

hi.why: Watch only the ball and you miss the change. You hit your usual shot into the new formation.
hi.caption: Beaten by a two-up volley

C5-01.coach: Watch who's moving and you'll see the formation.
C5-01.next: Where to hit against one up, one back?

C5-02.title: Beating one up, one back: where to hit?
C5-02.scene: One opponent is at the net, the other at the back.
C5-02.cue: The net player is in front of you; the back player is crosscourt.
C5-02.question: Where do you hit it?

answer.why: Against one up, one back, drive it deep to the back player. You avoid the net player and pin the back one.
answer.caption: You pinned the back player

lo.why: Their feet are a good target, but from the back the ball tends to float and get picked off.
lo.caption: The net player blocks it back

hi.why: With a net player standing there, the middle is theirs. It gets cut off.
hi.caption: Cut off in the middle

C5-02.coach: Against one up, one back, push the back player.

C5-03.title: After breaking one up, one back: your spot
C5-03.scene: Your deep ball pushed the back player out past the line.
C5-03.cue: The opponent leans back to hit it.
C5-03.question: Where do you go?

answer.why: Once you've pushed the back player out, move forward. Take the net side by side with your partner.
answer.caption: You took the net side by side

lo.why: Not bad, but you let the opening slip by.
lo.caption: You let the opening go

hi.short: All the way to the net at once
hi.why: Sprint all the way in and a lob goes right over your head.
hi.caption: Lobbed over

C5-03.coach: Broke them down? Move up together, side by side.

C5-04.title: Beating two up: first and second choice
C5-04.scene: Both opponents came forward, but not all the way to the net.
C5-04.cue: Both are standing near the service line.
C5-04.question: Where do you hit it?

answer.short: Low between them, at their feet
answer.why: Two up but far from the net leaves their feet open. Drop it low between them.
answer.caption: Broke them down at their feet

lo.why: Usually the first choice, but against players far from the net a lob tends to land short.
lo.caption: They back up and hit it

hi.why: Waist-high straight at them comes right back as a volley.
hi.caption: It came back as a volley

C5-04.coach: Two up but far back? Go for the feet first.

C5-05.title: Beating two back: draw them in short
C5-05.scene: Both opponents are staying on the baseline. You get an easy ball.
C5-05.cue: The front of their court is wide open.
C5-05.question: Where do you hit it?

answer.short: Short crosscourt to draw them in
answer.why: With both back, the front is open. Draw them in short and their formation falls apart.
answer.caption: You drew them in and finished it

lo.why: Safe, but with both back they return it comfortably.
lo.caption: They return it comfortably

hi.why: With both at the back, a deep ball goes right to them. The corner is easy to miss, too.
hi.caption: Went for the corner — out

C5-05.coach: Against two back, draw them in short.
C5-05.next: And after you draw them in?

C5-06.title: After drawing them in, we move up
C5-06.scene: Your short crosscourt pulled the opponent forward.
C5-06.cue: The opponent runs in and bends their knees.
C5-06.question: Where do you go?

answer.short: Close in at the net, side by side
answer.why: A player pulled in has to scoop the ball up. Move in so you can hit it from above.
answer.caption: You moved up and finished it

lo.why: Not bad, but you let the floater bounce and it's a rally again.
lo.caption: It's a rally again

hi.why: Draw them in and then back off, and you can't reach the short ball.
hi.caption: It dropped short

C5-06.coach: You drew them in — now we move in.
C5-06.next: Signs that attack is turning to defense

C5-07.title: From attack to defense: three signs
C5-07.scene: Your partner's volley floated up high. The opponent is set and waiting.
C5-07.cue: The opponent stands tall with the racket raised high.
C5-07.question: How will the next ball come?

answer.why: The ball floated, they're set, and the racket is high. See all three signs and it's time to defend.
answer.caption: You backed off and blocked it

lo.why: It could happen, but with all three signs it usually comes hard.
lo.caption: You barely blocked it

hi.why: A player who's set has no reason to hit soft. Move in and it's right at you.
hi.caption: Hit right at you

C5-07.coach: Ball up, opponent set, racket high — defend.

C5-08.title: From defense to attack: three signs
C5-08.scene: Your low ball landed at the opponent's feet.
C5-08.cue: The opponent is almost kneeling to dig it out.
C5-08.question: How will the next ball come?

answer.why: They're hitting low, leaning, with an open racket face. Three signs — switch to attack.
answer.caption: You switched to attack

lo.why: It could, but a ball dug out low usually floats. You're just waiting for a chance.
lo.caption: You just hit it back

hi.why: Someone digging it out low can't hit hard. Back off and the floater drops in front of you.
hi.caption: It dropped in front of you

C5-08.coach: Low and leaning? Time to attack.

C5-09.title: You saw the signs — what changes?
C5-09.scene: Your volley floated and the opponent is set. That's a defense sign.
C5-09.cue: Their racket is up over their head.
C5-09.question: What do you change?

answer.short: Both back off and hit high
answer.why: When you see the defense sign, change your position and your shot together. Both back off and lift it high.
answer.caption: You changed spot and shot

lo.why: You backed off right, but your partner stays up and you're split diagonally.
lo.caption: You barely held them off

hi.why: See the signs and stay put, and you're a smash target.
hi.caption: The smash slammed in

C5-09.coach: See the sign? Change it together.

C5-10.title: Keep hitting to the weak player?
C5-10.scene: You hit to the weak back player three times and won all three.
C5-10.cue: Their net player is creeping toward the middle.
C5-10.question: Where do you hit it?

answer.why: Keep hammering the weakness. But the net player is closing in, so go deeper and wider.
answer.caption: Broke them down again

lo.short: Switch to the net player's feet
lo.why: Mixing it up is good, but the strong net player is likely to block it.
lo.caption: The strong one blocks it

hi.short: Weak side, short to the middle
hi.why: Go into the middle where the net player is closing in and it gets cut off.
hi.caption: Cut off by the net player

C5-10.coach: Hammer the weakness, but away from the net player.
C5-10.next: After the same shot three times?

C5-11.title: After the same shot three times
C5-11.scene: You hit the same crosscourt three times. Now they're there early.
C5-11.cue: The back player is already waiting near the crosscourt corner.
C5-11.question: Where do you hit it?

answer.why: Change a shot they've read. The back player is in the corner, so the middle is open.
answer.caption: Into the open middle

lo.why: It might work, but that's where they're already waiting.
lo.caption: They were waiting for it

hi.short: Down the line at the net player
hi.why: The net player is still standing there. Down the line is right in front of their racket.
hi.caption: The net player picked it off

C5-11.coach: Same shot three times? Change the fourth.
C5-11.next: What if the net player moves first?

C5-12.title: They've read your pattern
C5-12.scene: Every time the ball went left you followed, and twice they passed you on the right.
C5-12.cue: The opponent is watching the side you leave open.
C5-12.question: Where do you go this time?

answer.why: Following is right, but go all the way and you leave a hole. Go only to the middle.
answer.caption: You caught the ball they aimed

lo.why: You cover your side, but this time the middle opens.
lo.caption: Your partner barely gets it

hi.why: Follow all the way and the spot they were aiming for opens up again.
hi.caption: Passed on the right again

C5-12.coach: If they've read you, follow only halfway.
C5-12.next: What if your partner keeps getting passed?

C5-13.title: Planning a point: serve, poach, finish
C5-13.scene: As planned, your partner served down the T. Your turn to poach.
C5-13.cue: The returner swings crosscourt from the middle.
C5-13.question: Where do you hit from, and where to?

answer.short: Middle, at the net player's feet
answer.why: A return off a T serve comes through the middle. Cut it off and put it at the nearest player's feet.
answer.caption: Finished as planned

lo.why: Break the plan and your partner has to take it alone.
lo.caption: The plan fell apart

hi.why: Leave before the serve and the returner sees it and goes down the line. Go the moment they hit the return.
hi.caption: Passed down the open line

C5-13.coach: A planned poach starts on the return.

C5-14.title: Hit it here — where does it come back?
C5-14.scene: Both opponents were back, so you went deep down the middle.
C5-14.cue: The opponent is hitting from the very center of the court.
C5-14.question: Where will they hit it?

answer.why: From the middle there's no angle. The ball usually comes back to the middle.
answer.caption: You were already in the middle

lo.why: It could happen, but a lob from the middle tends to be short.
lo.caption: You back up and barely get it

hi.why: There's no angle for the line from the middle. Cover your side and the middle opens.
hi.caption: It went through the middle

C5-14.coach: Send it down the middle and it comes back down the middle.
C5-14.next: How do you cover their answer early?

C5-15.title: The spot that covers their answer
C5-15.scene: Both opponents are back, and you get a high ball.
C5-15.cue: The front right of their court is wide open.
C5-15.question: Where do you go after you hit?

answer.short: Angle it right, then to the middle
answer.why: Pull them out with an angle and they answer crosscourt or down the line. Your partner covers the line; you cover the middle.
answer.caption: You covered their answer

lo.why: A good angle, but you're both late on an answer through the middle.
lo.caption: You barely covered it

hi.why: Pull them in and then back off, and a short answer drops in front of you.
hi.caption: Beaten by a short answer

C5-15.coach: Before you hit, cover their answer.

C5-16.title: The net player moved early: go the other way
C5-16.scene: You're about to hit a fourth crosscourt, and the net player moves first.
C5-16.cue: The net player leaves for the middle before the ball does.
C5-16.question: Where do you hit it?

answer.why: If they guess and move early, the other side opens. That's when you go down the line.
answer.caption: Passed them the other way

lo.why: A good ball might work, but the net player is already in the path.
lo.caption: The net player barely touches it

hi.why: Hit to where the net player is going and it's cut off.
hi.caption: Cut off

C5-16.coach: Net player moved early? Go the other way.

C5-17.title: Your partner keeps getting passed
C5-17.scene: The opponent passed your partner down the line twice.
C5-17.cue: The opponent opens up toward the line again.
C5-17.question: Where do you go?

answer.short: Half a step behind your partner
answer.why: If your partner's side keeps getting passed, you back them up. Half a step and you can reach the line ball.
answer.caption: You backed up the line

lo.why: You hold your spot, but the line ball is too far.
lo.caption: You barely reach it from afar

hi.why: Your partner's back is open — go up too and the line is wide open.
hi.caption: Passed down the line again

C5-17.coach: If your partner gets passed, back them up.

C5-18.title: Should we try the Australian formation?
C5-18.scene: We keep losing to the returner's crosscourt return. Let's change formation.
C5-18.cue: The returner's crosscourt only goes toward our server.
C5-18.question: Where do you stand?

answer.short: At the net, on the server's side
answer.why: Stand in the crosscourt path and the returner has to switch to down the line. The server covers the left after serving.
answer.caption: You blocked the crosscourt path

lo.why: Familiar, but it leaves open the crosscourt you keep losing to.
lo.caption: Crosscourt again

hi.short: In the middle, ahead of time
hi.why: Standing halfway in the middle leaves the left line open. Commit to the formation.
hi.caption: Passed down the left line

C5-18.coach: Losing crosscourt? Stand in the crosscourt path.
C5-18.next: What about a day with wind and sun?

C5-19.title: Choosing your shot in wind and sun
C5-19.scene: A strong wind blows from their side toward ours.
C5-19.cue: Both opponents at the net are facing the sun.
C5-19.question: Where do you hit it?

answer.short: A high lob, down the middle
answer.why: Into the wind, a lob won't sail long. And a smash hit looking into the sun often misses.
answer.caption: Their smash missed

lo.why: A good play, but into the wind the ball sits up for an easy volley.
lo.caption: Volleyed back over

hi.why: Into the wind a hard ball slows and sits up for the net player. They put it away.
hi.caption: The slowed ball got picked off

C5-19.coach: Headwind and sun are on the lob's side.

C5-20.title: Planning a point in five shots
C5-20.scene: Wide serve, crosscourt return — all as planned. Now it's the third ball.
C5-20.cue: The returner is still recovering from out wide.
C5-20.question: Where do you go after you hit?

answer.why: Hit deep down the middle to the recovering returner, then finish the floater up front.
answer.caption: Finished as planned in five

lo.why: A good third ball, but stay back and you miss the floater. The plan goes all the way to the net.
lo.caption: You let the floater go

hi.short: Hard down the line, then charge
hi.why: Down the line is where the net player is standing. The plan breaks at the third ball.
hi.caption: The plan broke at ball three

C5-20.coach: The plan doesn't end at the third ball.

C5-21.title: Rally simulation A: three shots ahead
C5-21.scene: Your partner's deep crosscourt went to the back player's corner.
C5-21.cue: The back player turns into a crosscourt stance.
C5-21.question: Where will the next ball go?

answer.why: A back player pushed deep usually answers with the same crosscourt. The third ball is your poach.
answer.caption: You took the third ball

lo.why: It could come, but down the line is hard when you're pushed deep.
lo.caption: The crosscourt went past

hi.why: Pushed deep, their lob is short too. Back off and you miss the crosscourt through the middle.
hi.caption: It went through the middle

C5-21.coach: Push them deep, and the next crosscourt is yours.

C5-22.title: Rally simulation B
C5-22.scene: The opponent's back player got dragged out past the left corner.
C5-22.cue: The back right of their court is wide open.
C5-22.question: Where do you go after you hit?

answer.short: Into the open back, then middle
answer.why: The back corner opposite the dragged player is the widest gap. Hit it, then return to the middle.
answer.caption: Finished into the open back

lo.why: A good target, but you hit at a person when there was a bigger gap.
lo.caption: The net player blocks it back

hi.short: Back to the side they went
hi.why: Send it back to the player you dragged out and you give them time to recover.
hi.caption: Passed by the ball they sent back

C5-22.coach: Drag them out and the other side opens.

C5-23.title: Rally simulation C
C5-23.scene: While your partner is pulled out wide left, a ball comes down the middle.
C5-23.cue: Your partner is still on the way back.
C5-23.question: Where do you hit from, and how?

answer.short: Move to the middle, hit deep
answer.why: Buy time for your partner. Hit deep from the middle and you both get back in position.
answer.caption: You both got back in position

lo.short: A sharp angle to the side
lo.why: Nice angle, but it comes back fast into the open left.
lo.caption: It came back to the open left

hi.why: Hit hard at the net player and it comes back into the open left. Your partner isn't there yet.
hi.caption: Passed through the open left

C5-23.coach: If your partner's out, buy time.

C5-24.title: Final: the shot that ends this point
C5-24.scene: One opponent is at the net, the other is recovering from the right corner.
C5-24.cue: A high ball floats up in front of you.
C5-24.question: Where's the finishing shot?

answer.why: One is up, one is recovering. The space between them is the biggest gap in this point.
answer.caption: You ended the point

lo.why: A good target, but right now there's a bigger gap.
lo.caption: They block it back

hi.why: Send it to the recovering player and it's right on their path. You hand back the ball you should finish.
hi.caption: Sent right into their path

C5-24.coach: To finish, aim for the biggest gap right now.
